text:
Alex C: quick async check on the kernel-batching + KV cache sprint. TL;DR: need owners for the kernel perf PR, blocker list, and eng-infra CI merge ETA. Goal this week: ~15% p95 token latency drop on long contexts.

Maria P: working on the kernel loop refactor, PR is up at github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 — needs perf regression run and a second reviewer. Not ready to land until CI CUDA matrix is green.

Sam T: I can take review on the kernel side. Can someone confirm the target perf numbers? 15% p95 overall or for the attention kernel specifically?

Alex C: 15% p95 overall for generation workloads (seq=2048 baseline). If the attention kernel alone gives ~20% in microbench, that’s fine. We need end-to-end numbers before the canary.

Maria P: noted. I ran local bench (small dataset) — about 12% p95 improvement so far. Will run the full harness tomorrow.

Jin L: eng-infra update: CUDA CI changes are in the infra branch, still blocked by the new docker runner permissions. ETA EOD tomorrow to unblock, unless we hit more policy issues. 

Alex C: @Jin L thanks. If infra thinks it might slip, we should have a fallback plan to run full perf in a preprod cluster manually.

Sam T: I’ll prep a canary job that runs the PR on a dedicated preprod GPU pool. If infra blocks the CI merge, we can run that job and post results. Need someone to grant me pool access or a token.

Maria P: @Sam T I can run the canary if you send the job config. Here’s the small kernel config I used locally: 
```yaml
kernel:
  continuous_batching: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  prefer_small_kernels: false
kv_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 3600
  shard_count: 4
  read_path: "shared"
```

Maria P: also small patch to reduce locking contention — quick diff: 
```diff
- kv_read_lock();
+ kv_read_lock_shared();
```

Alex C: nice. Add that diff to the PR description and tag @sam for relevant lines.

Sam T: pinged on the PR. I see the diff; quick question — does the shared lock change preserve correctness under concurrent writes?

Maria P: yes — writes still take exclusive lock. Shared lock only for reads to avoid stalling generation paths. I added unit tests for this.

Jin L: infra: if you need pool access, submit an access request (tools/internal/gpu-access) and cc me, I’ll expedite. Also we need the quick CI command for those running tests locally: `./tools/ci/run_cuda_tests.sh --quick --tag=kernel`

Alex C: action items: 1) Maria finish full harness run + attach numbers to PR (owner: Maria). 2) Sam review and approve or call out blockers (owner: Sam). 3) Jin unblock CI or approve pool access (owner: Jin). 4) If CI slips, run preprod canary (backup: Sam+Maria).

Sam T: okay I’ll do a review pass tomorrow morning. If I see anything risky I’ll flag for a short design sync.

Maria P: FYI I saw a small memory regression on long sequences in one test — investigating whether it’s the batching heuristic. I’ll post a minimal repro later.

Alex C: please add repro and a perf trace (flame graph) to the PR when you have it. That helps us decide canary thresholds.

deploy-bot: build/runtime-pr-1892 started by Maria P — status: queued. (link: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/1892)

Sam T: got the CI link, thanks. I’ll follow the run and annotate the PR with expected signal checks: p95, memory, and kv miss rate.

Maria P: quick note on rollout strategy: if kernel PR lands we’ll A/B route 10% traffic to new kernel variant for 24h with canary metrics (latency, correctness, OOMs). Canary config lives in ops/canaries/kernel_canary.yaml.

Alex C: sounds good. last ask — please ping me on Slack when PR is reviewed+CI green so I can schedule the canary rollout. :thumbsup:

Sam T: will do.

Maria P: posting the minimal repro shortly. Thanks everyone.
